head:

Twenty-eight deputy collectors of internal revenue named in letter of the
Secretary of the Treasury dated March 8, 1917, appointed without reference to
the civil service rules under authority of the act of October 22, 1913, may be
transferred to competitive classified positions of field deputy collector, income
tax roll, to serve until not later than August 31, 1917. Owing to the demand
for war munitions, there has been a heavy increase in the production of tax-
free alcohol. This has made necessary the employment of an unusual number
of storekeepers and gaugers, with the result that the appropriation from which
storekeeper-gaugers and agents are paid has been depleted to a point where a
deficiency of considerable magnitude is threatened, notwithstanding the utmost
reduction of the force of storekeeper-gaugers. This deficiency can be averted
only by the transfer of the force known as " special gaugers " (storekeeper-
gaugers assigned to special duty under division revenue agents) to the deputy
collector roll. By transferring them to positions as general deputy collectors on
the regular roil, the storekeeper-gaugers-agents appropriation can be relieved.
It is desired to transfer deputy collectors appointed without examination but
assigned to income tax work to the income tax roll.
This will enable the Treasury Department to utilize the several separate
appropriations from which the field force of the Internal Revenue Service is
paid, and to thus continue the se

Mr. William J. Martin may be appointed to a competitive position in the
Treasury Department.

of law to secure the more expeditious distribution of valuable seeds authorized by
law, and by virtue of the authority vested in me by the provisions of the Act
of Congress approved March 4, 1917, entitled "An Act making appropriations
for the naval service for the fiscal year ending June thirtieth, nineteen hundred
and eighteen, and for other purposes," whereby it is provided "That in case
of national emergency the President is authorized to suspend provisions of law
prohibiting more than eight hours labor in any one day of persons engaged

machine_read.last_words: from and after this date WOODROW WILSON THE WHITE HOUSE April No

head:
]Erecutt'e 'rber,
Whereas, the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of
America, in Congress assembled, have declared that a state of war exists between
the United States and the Imperial German Government; and
Whereas it is necessary to operate certain radio stations for radio communi-
cation by the Government and to close other radio stations not so operated, to
insure the proper conduct of the war against the Imperial German Government
and the successful termination thereof
Now, therefore, it is ordered by virtue of authority vested in me by the Act
to Regulate Radio Communication, approved August 13, 1912, that such radio
stations within the jurisdiction of the United States as are required for naval
communications shall be taken over by the Government of the United States
and used and controlled by it, to the exclusion of any other control or use;
and furthermore that all radio stations not necessary to the Government of the
United States for naval communications, may be closed for radio communi-
cation.
The enforcement of this order is hereby delegated to the Secretary of the
Navy, who is authorized and directed to take such action in the premises as
to him may appear necessary.
This order shall take effect from and after this date.t
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
6 April, r1917.
[No. 2585.]

harbors, and canals. In addition to his large experience in river and harbor
work, he has passed several high grade examinations for responsible positions
in the classified service. His services are urgently required in connection with
the completion of the survey of the Arkansas River, a difficult work and one
which cannot be satisfactorily performed except by a person having broad
experience.
The Civil Service Commission joins with the Secretary of War in recom-
mending this order.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
i6 April, 1917.
[No. 2598.]
